Withings "profiles" yaml configuration is no longer supported and has been moved into ui-based configuration.


## Proposed change
<!-- 
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
The Withings "profiles" config attribute is largely unnecessary, confuses users and requires you restart home assistant when you need to add a new person. For these reasons, it has been removed in favor of the user providing their own name at the end of setup.

issue_context.title: Withings only supports one account (not profile)
issue_context.body:
<!-- READ THIS FIRST:
  - If you need additional help with this template, please refer to https://www.home-assistant.io/help/reporting_issues/
  - Make sure you are running the latest version of Home Assistant before reporting an issue: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/releases
  - Do not report issues for integrations if you are using custom components or integrations.
  - Provide as many details as possible. Paste logs, configuration samples and code into the backticks.
  DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! Otherwise, your issue may be closed without comment.
-->
## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened.
-->
The Withings integration supports only a single account, despite the fact that users of Withings devices within the same household have individual accounts. Note: this is not about multiple profiles on a single account, but individual accounts linked to the same device.

## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Developer tools -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: all versions (0.110 tested)
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): none
- Operating environment (Home Assistant/Supervised/Docker/venv): Docker
- Integration causing this issue: Withings
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/withings/

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
<!--
  An example configuration that caused the problem for you. Fill this out even
  if it seems unimportant to you. Please be sure to remove personal information
  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->

```yaml
withings:
  client_id: !secret withings_client_id
  client_secret: !secret withings_consumer_secret
  profiles:
    - UserA
    - UserB
```

Also attempted the normal way to use things twice:

```yaml
withings accountA:
  client_id: !secret withings_client_id
  client_secret: !secret withings_consumer_secret
  profiles:
    - UserA

withings accountB:
  client_id: !secret withings_client_id_b
  client_secret: !secret withings_consumer_secret_b
  profiles:
    - UserB
```

## Traceback/Error logs
<!--
  If you come across any trace or error logs, please provide them.
-->

```txt

```

## Additional information
comments:
Hey there @vangorra, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with a integration (`withings`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L460) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

Support for multiple accounts and UI based setup is the next big change for the withings integration. Once #34447 is merged, we can begin work. Note: That PR includes a lot of necessary fixes in addition to webhook support.

BTW. The current withings integration does not limit you to 1 account. Those profile in the config are arbitrary. There's nothing stopping you from creating a profile named 'profile from another account'. Then when adding the integration, you are taken to the withings site, from there you, logout from the current account and login to the preferred one and continue the process.

But then the other account would have a different `client_id` and `client_secret`; are these used _only_ for initial authentication? How is authentication handled after the fact? Credentials stored in the .storage?

`client_id` and `client_secret` are credentials for your Withings developer account. This is not the consumer's user account. Developer accounts allow apps to access consumer data (when approved by the user). With proper authorization, the developer account could access any withings consumer account.
All that being said. I'm going to remove the profiles list from the withings config once the webhooks PR is merged. This has caused more confusion that it's worth.

Thanks. I see the PR, but I finally got around to trying what you suggested, and it worked flawlessly.

I'd offer to update the documentation, but it seems like the PR changes everything.

Because, strictly speaking, this issue is resolved (doesn't exist; user error), I'll close this.

review_comments: The `CONF_PROFILES` item needs to still be part of the dict schema, as optional, to not make it invalid when that item is included.
I pushed something different, let me know if this is correct. I'm not entirely sure how the deprecated option values work. HASS contains many examples with various usage but it's still unclear to me.

I know the webhook ID stuff is not part of this PR, I just noticed this now.

This fixes a change in the data schema of tne configuration entry. This should have been done using a config entry migration.
Could you be a bit more specific? I'm not sure what to fix.
The downside of a migration of the config entry is that it makes it impossible to roll back to an earlier home assistant version.
@MartinHjelmare Basically, the same thing is happening here. The schema is changed/migrated... ?

In this case we don't seem to change the structure of the existing entry data, so here it doesn't matter what migration approach we take I think.

What I meant was that if the existing data is moved to a different structure in the entry data, a rollback is not possible. As long as we're only adding items to the root level of the dict and don't touch the existing root level items, a rollback is possible.

The code was changed because `ConfigFlow.async_set_unique_id()` expects a string for the `unique_id` and I figured this should be updated to stay consistent with the rest of the HASS code base.
Should this be changed/removed?

I think it is fine to leave as is right now. I just noticed it and is out of scope for this PR I would say. 👍 

Let's resolve this conversation for now and focus on the actually PR 😉

Removing this, causes a hard breaking change: The configuration becomes invalid if one has this in its configuration.

Another alternative approach: Mark `CONF_PROFILES` as deprecated. It would still be allowed in the config, would throw a warning in the logs and for the code, you can just ignore it.

Remove the deprecation notice after a couple of releases.
